q: Fossil fuels, such as coal, oil and natural gas, are important ____ sources of energy.
e: Fossil fuels are classified as non-renewable because they take millions of years to form.

q: ____ is the main constituent of these fossil fuels.
e: Carbon is the primary chemical element found in all fossil fuels.

q: A large amount of ____ energy is stored in the fossil fuels.
e: Fossil fuels store energy in the form of chemical bonds.

q: Fossil fuels are excellent sources of energy for our ____ needs.
e: Refined fossil fuels like gasoline are predominantly used for transportation.

q: Fossil fuel liquids also are refined into ____ products that are used as ingredients in the manufacture of literally hundreds of products from plastics and polyurethane to solvents.
e: Petrochemicals are derived from fossil fuels and used to manufacture plastics and solvents.

q: Coal is formed in a way similar to the other fossil fuels, though it goes through a different process called ____.
e: Coalification is the specific geological process that turns plant matter into coal.

q: It is made of ____ plant matter in conditions of high temperature and pressure, and it takes a relatively shorter amount of time to form.
e: Coal originates from the decomposed remains of ancient plant matter.

q: ____ is another major source of the energy in our country.
e: Natural gas is a significant fossil fuel energy source extracted from underground fields.

q: These fields always contain some gases, but this natural gas (____) does not take nearly as long to form.
e: The primary chemical component of natural gas is methane.

q: Methane is a common gas found in swamps and is also the by-product of animals' ____ system.
e: Methane is naturally produced during the digestive processes of many animals.

q: Nuclear energy is non-renewable as the uranium fuels used are consumed in the nuclear ____ reaction and hence are non-replenishable.
e: Nuclear power plants generate energy through the fission of uranium atoms.

q: Nevertheless, nuclear energy has many uses: energy produced in a nuclear ____ can be harnessed to produce electricity.
e: A nuclear reactor is the facility where nuclear fission is controlled to produce heat.

q: Nuclear energy is also being used to power ____ and ship.
e: Nuclear propulsion allows submarines to operate for long periods without refueling.

q: ____ obtained as by-products in nuclear reactions are used in medicine, agriculture and research.
e: Radioisotopes are valuable by-products of nuclear reactions used across various scientific fields.
